findings.evidence: containment.ts:14 `if (path !== "/api/health/quick-order" && !path.startsWith("/api/health/quick-order/")) next()`; server/index.ts@4abd2c5:321-331 express.json verify sets req.rawBody for every JSON request that reaches it; :1494 `/api/{*rest}` 404 is reached after parsing. The leading-slash normalizer (:231-236) only collapses a leading run. containment.test.ts@4abd2c5 covers //, absolute-form and fragment targets but no case or interior-slash variant. Today nothing downstream logs or stores such a body (request-logging.ts:6-14 exact SAFE set; apiLogPath -> /api/[redacted]; error handler never copies request values), so this is parse-then-discard, not a leak. The legacy idiom (server/research/index.ts:70-87, app.post('/api/research/orders')) inherits Express's case-insensitive matching.

findings.claim: requestUrl() throws InputError(400,'invalid_request') for any originalUrl that starts with '//' or is not '/'-prefixed BEFORE ownsPath() decides whether the request belongs to the quick-order namespace, and the catch at :205-206 sends the 400 instead of calling next(). Mounted at the application root as docs/INTEGRATION.md:31-42 requires (and as the handler's own next-fallthrough design assumes), every site request whose originalUrl is '//research/...', '//api/research/...' or an absolute-form target would receive a quick-order JSON 400 instead of reaching its real route or the SPA.

Express sets originalUrl before the host normalizer at server/index.ts:231-236 rewrites req.url, and containment.test.ts:63 observes originalUrl retaining the '//' form. Add a test: `invoke('//other')` and an absolute-form target must call next(), and `invoke('//api/health/quick-order/requests')` must still refuse.

findings.claim: The default-off containment compares the raw Express req.path string, while the handler it stands in for compares the WHATWG-normalized `new URL(raw, origin).pathname`. The two disagree on dot-segments and backslashes: `/api/health/x/../quick-order/requests` and `/api/health/quick-order\requests` are NOT contained (req.path keeps them literally; Express 5 and Node's parser do not normalize them), so the body reaches express.json (2 MB limit, req.rawBody retained for the request at server/index.ts:322-331) and then the `/api/{*rest}` 404 at :1494, whereas the future root-mounted handler would normalize both to `/api/health/quick-order/requests` and own them. This is the same bypass class the coordinator already required fixing for '//' (QUALIFICATION.md:10-16). It is not a data leak: no persistence, and the request logger labels the path `/api/[redacted]` (server/request-logging.ts:46) with no body capture; but it defeats the stated purpose of the boundary ('terminate before any application body parser or rawBody verifier can retain customer-supplied bytes').

WHATWG URL path state removes `..` segments and treats `\` as `/` for special schemes; parseurl (req.path) does neither. containment.test.ts:43-105 covers exact, '//', absolute-form, fragment and oversized cases, but no `..` or `\` case. The patch mounts at server/index.ts after line 275 (MOUNT_PROPOSAL.patch:105-106), i.e. after the '//' normalizer (231-236) and before express.json (322) -- placement is correct; the predicate is the gap.

Simplest: containment computes `new URL(req.url, 'https://quick-order.invalid').pathname` (catching parse failure as 'not ours' -> next, or as 'contained' if the raw target starts with the literal prefix) and the handler uses the same helper; add containment tests for `/api/health/x/../quick-order/requests`, `/api/health/quick-order\requests` and `/api/health/quick-order/%2e%2e/requests` asserting parserReached/verifierReached are not called.
